The Second Life viewer with a studio inside: shape, paint and fire your work without leaving the world.
See it in-world before you upload
First, shape it right where it stands.
Then open it flat and mark the seams.
Then paint the glaze on the cup itself.
Then fire it and set it on the table.
Turn on JavaScript to paint the tile.
Paint straight onto the face in-world, in layers, with base colour, roughness and emission. Try it on the test tile.
Select vertices, edges or faces on the object in-world and move, extrude or cut them.
Unwrap, pack and see the seams on the object while you work, not in a separate program.
Levels of detail for the example cup
Generate all four levels of detail and the physics shape, and read the land impact before you pay to upload.
Wear and rez your work locally, with your own textures, until it is right. Upload once, at the end.
For the big jobs, send the mesh to Blender and back as glTF, without exporting by hand.

Kiln starts from Linden Lab’s own viewer and follows its releases, so new Second Life features arrive with each merge. It keeps its own settings and cache, and runs beside Firestorm or the official viewer.
A kiln is where shaped clay and wet glaze become one finished piece. That is the step Kiln brings into the viewer.
Yes. Kiln is free, and its source is released under LGPL-2.1, the same licence as the viewer it is built on.
There is no public build yet. Follow the Kiln organisation on GitHub to hear when the first preview is ready.
Do I have to give up Firestorm?
No. Kiln has its own install folder, settings and cache, so it runs beside Firestorm or the official viewer.
For big modelling jobs, yes. Kiln covers the changes you make between uploads, and the Blender link carries the mesh across and back.
Painting and previewing stay on your computer. You pay Second Life’s usual fee only when you upload the finished texture or mesh.
Is Kiln made by Linden Lab?
No. Kiln is an independent third-party viewer, built to follow Linden Lab’s Third Party Viewer Policy. It is not made or endorsed by Linden Lab.
